clue.text: Athlete with golf shot of the highest quality

blocks.note: a Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
a short lofted shot onto the green

explanation.surface: A sporting star with a superb golf stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson, a British university honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip describes stocks or companies regarded as the most reliable and valuable, hence top grade.

clue.text: British countess on stage in foreign country

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Olivia is the countess in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A British aristocrat performing in a theatre abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a South American nation, so foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a French business

blocks.note: the French masculine word for a
a concern is a firm or enterprise

explanation.surface: Someone is indifferent to a company in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is indifference, an absence of worry or engagement with something.

clue.text: Church has way, in general, to make organ stop

indicators.note: one item placed inside another is literally in it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Church of England
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A church gets its way generally, producing a stop on its organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads like a phrase meaning mostly, but 'general' is a soldier and 'in' puts the way inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste (voix céleste) is a soft, slightly detuned stop found on pipe organs.

clue.text: Such characters are inclined to be emphatic

definitions.text: Such characters are inclined to be emphatic

blocks.clueFragment: Such characters are inclined to be emphatic
blocks.note: surface reading: people who tend to speak forcefully
setter's reading: printed letters that slope, used for emphasis in text

explanation.definitionFit: Italic type leans to the right and is used to stress words, so these letters are literally sloping and emphatic.

clue.text: Angelic being, extremely serene with harp, possibly

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only its outer letters are kept
possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: first and last letters of serene
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavenly figure, wholly calm, with a harp in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Son with poor instructor is dull-witted type

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
poor in quality, as in low marks
a coach trains or teaches

explanation.surface: A boy taught badly turns out to be slow on the uptake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a person who acts or thinks sluggishly, so a slow-minded sort.

clue.text: Fraudulent schemes providing sport for court

blocks.note: first meaning: dishonest money-making operations
second meaning: a ball game played against walls in an enclosed court

explanation.surface: Swindles that give a law court something to enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a law court, which fits the fraud; it is the walled court the game is played in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rackets are both criminal swindles and a fast indoor ball game, forerunner of squash.

clue.text: Characters from Dickens and Austen meeting in afternoon once

blocks.note: Pip is the hero of Great Expectations
Emma Woodhouse, heroine of Emma

explanation.surface: Fictional figures from two novelists come together.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip emma is old British military signallers' talk for p.m., P and M spoken in the phonetic alphabet of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Pip emma was a dated spoken form of p.m., meaning after noon, now obsolete.

clue.text: Form of entertainment set in pub?

definitions.text: Form of entertainment set in pub?

blocks.clueFragment: Form of entertainment set in pub?
blocks.note: surface reading: a show staged inside a bar
setter's reading: a wireless set, placed in a local, the British word for a neighbourhood pub

explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British pub near home; a set is an old word for a receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Community broadcasting stations serving one area are a familiar form of entertainment and information.

clue.text: Reserved outside page for newspaper material

indicators.note: one word goes outside, around, the other, wrapping it

blocks.note: coy means shy or reticent
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A seat set aside beyond a page of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy is the written text supplied to be printed in a newspaper by journalists.

clue.text: Suspect cat burglar of taking this cosmetic?

definitions.text: Suspect cat burglar of taking this cosmetic?

blocks.clueFragment: Suspect cat burglar of taking this cosmetic?
blocks.note: surface reading: a thief is thought to have stolen a beauty product
setter's reading: a burglar disappearing with the good stuff, the cream of the loot

explanation.walkthrough: Cream is both a cosmetic and the best of something, and a burglar who is vanishing has made off.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a light face cream that seems to disappear into the skin when applied.

clue.text: Not getting on, apparently, in language lessons

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follow, spanning them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone making no progress in their language classes.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting on means growing old, so not getting on is staying young; 'apparently' admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never seems to grow older, so it is not visibly advancing in years.

clue.text: Protection for guard making second appearance to fight

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
an entrance onto a scene
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A shield for a soldier coming back for a second bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry box is a small shelter in which a sentinel stands on duty.

clue.text: Tool that can get nails out

blocks.note: first meaning: a person used by another, a dupe
second meaning: a cat's foot, which extends its claws; also a claw-ended bar for pulling nails

explanation.walkthrough: A tool is also a person used by others, and the fable has a monkey use a cat's limb to pull chestnuts from the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's paw is a dupe exploited by another, and also a claw-ended bar for extracting nails.

clue.text: Prophet supporting king about proclamation

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the last one

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
Rex, king
an official decree

explanation.surface: A seer backing a monarch over an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces join before wrapping the decree, and the split falls after their second letter, not at the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A predictor foretells what will happen, which is what a prophet does.

clue.text: Continuous management

blocks.note: first meaning: in succession
second meaning: the operation or control of a business

explanation.definitionFit: The word means consecutive or ongoing, and as a noun the day-to-day control of an organisation.

clue.text: As a rule, uranium's held by European member of NATO?

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped within it, so one goes inside

blocks.note: chemical symbol
a European NATO member is an ally of America

explanation.surface: Normally, a European NATO state keeps a stock of nuclear fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means is: uranium is held by a US ally, giving US(U)ALLY. The question mark flags the cryptic description.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually means normally or in most cases, which is what as a rule expresses.

clue.text: Harbour here unsuitable for old vessels?

definitions.text: Harbour here unsuitable for old vessels?

blocks.clueFragment: Harbour here unsuitable for old vessels?
blocks.note: surface reading: a dock that cannot take ancient ships
setter's reading: a place name that splits into a fresh harbour, which by name suits only fresh ones

explanation.walkthrough: Newport is a town in South Wales with docks; read as two words it is a harbour that is new.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is a real port town, and its name literally describes a recently built harbour.

clue.text: Shatters in quakes

blocks.note: first meaning: breaks into fragments
second meaning: trembles with cold or fear

explanation.surface: Something breaks apart during earth tremors.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver is to smash into splinters and also to tremble, two unrelated verbs with one spelling.

clue.text: One larks about stupidly without a breathing apparatus

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is dropped
fooling around stupidly means acting in disorder, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: A person fooling about with no air supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a tube letting a swimmer draw air while face down in water.

clue.text: Hide his notice - the contents are so stupid

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so each word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: inner letters
inner letter
inner letters

explanation.surface: Conceal that man's announcement, since what it says is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means extremely foolish, a close synonym for brainless or dim.

clue.text: Provide time to stop supply of drink

blocks.note: first meaning: state at what moment, literally
second meaning: the host's invitation to signal enough has been poured

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase asks someone to name a moment; idiomatically it asks a guest to halt the pouring.

clue.text: Increasing affluence due to getting a rise?

definitions.text: Increasing affluence due to getting a rise?

blocks.clueFragment: Increasing affluence due to getting a rise?
blocks.note: surface reading: becoming richer thanks to a pay increase
setter's reading: a social climb, ascent through the classes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names movement into a higher social or economic class, typically with more money.

clue.text: Muse about painting worked on by Turner?

indicators.note: a turner turns things, so this painting is flipped round end to end

blocks.note: circa
an oil is a painting

explanation.surface: An inspiring spirit considers a canvas the great painter Turner laboured on.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner suggests J.M.W. Turner the painter, which suits oils; here it is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over history.

clue.text: Pain on rear that's produced by needle

blocks.note: the back is the rear
a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: An ache in one's behind caused by a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' puts the first piece after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstitch is a sewing stitch made with a needle, overlapping the previous one.

clue.text: Offence said to strain rules for sentences

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is wanted for its sound

blocks.note: a sin is a moral offence
to tax is to put a strain on

explanation.surface: A crime supposedly puts a burden on the legal rules for prison terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Sentences look legal, after offence; they are grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the set of grammatical principles governing how words combine into sentences.

clue.text: Sort of microscope chosen by short chap

blocks.note: elect as an adjective means picked
Ron is a short form of Ronald

explanation.surface: A microscope picked out by a small man.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron microscope uses a beam of particles instead of light to magnify, so it names a kind.
